Diarrhea (often

2-5 days after

Drinking raw milk or eating raw or under-
cooked meat, shellfish, or poultry; to pre-
vent exposure, avoid raw milk and cook all 
meats and poultry thoroughly; it is safest to 
drink only pasteurized milk; the bacteria also 
may be found in tofu or raw vegetables.
Hand-washing is important for prevention; 
wash hands with soap before handling 
raw foods of animal origin, after handling 
raw foods of animal origin, and before 
touching anything else; prevent cross- 
contamination in the kitchen; proper refrig-
eration and sanitation are also essential.
Top source of foodborne illness; some 
people develop antibodies to it, but 
others do not. In persons with com-
promised immune systems, it may 
spread to the bloodstream and 
cause sepsis; may lead to arthritis 
or to GBS; 40% of GBS in the 
United States is caused by campylo-
bacteriosis and affects the nerves of 
the body, beginning several weeks 
after the diarrheal illness; can lead 
to paralysis that lasts several weeks 
and usually requires intensive care.
